# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 3 THE LAND OF DREAMS AMONG

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Nell, have you decided whom you will invite to the wedding?” inquired Mrs. Agatha Sowerby, while she busily hemstitched table napkins. “Even if they are just going to be informal, it is time for your invitations to go out.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0000 }

“It is not my intention to have a large number,” Nell remarked. “Our desire is simply for those held dearest by us to witness our wedding. The family of Hugh, along with Mr. and Mrs. Wace, plus Mr. and Mrs. Pettifer.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0001 }

“You would scarcely have counted Mr. Pettifer as one of your closest companions in the past,” Thirza remarked drily.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0002 }

“Indeed, I did not feel a VERY powerful draw toward him when we first met,” admitted Nell, laughing as she remembered it. “However, getting to know Mr. Pettifer better has raised my opinion of him, while Mrs. Pettifer is truly sweet. Additionally, we must not forget Miss Rosalind and Cedric.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0003 }

“Did they make up their minds to visit the Island during this summer? It was my understanding that they intended to travel to Europe.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0004 }

“Their perspective shifted once my letter informed them of my upcoming marriage. A communication from Cedric arrived for me today. He states that he MUST attend my wedding, regardless of the situation in Europe.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0005 }

“You were always idolised by that child,” Mrs. Agatha remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0006 }

“Mrs. Sowerby, that ‘child’ has grown into a nineteen-year-old young man now.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0007 }

“How time does fly!” was the brilliant and original reply made by Mrs. Sowerby.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0008 }

“Belinda the Fourth might accompany them. Through Cedric, she passed along word that she would attend provided her husband allowed it. I ponder if those huge blue bows are still worn by her, and if she is addressed by her husband as Belinda or Leonora. Having Belinda present at my wedding would be a delight for me. A long time ago, a wedding was attended by Belinda and me. At Echo Cottage, their arrival is anticipated next week. Additionally, Cressy and the Reverend Ez—— are expected”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0009 }

“It sounds terrible to hear you talk about a clergyman in such a manner, Nell,” Mrs. Agatha remarked sternly.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0010 }

“He is called that by his wife.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0011 }

“Then she ought to show greater reverence for his sacred calling,” Mrs. Agatha fired back.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0012 }

“I’ve listened to you rebuke clergymen rather severely on your own,” Nell jested.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0013 }

“Yes, but my actions are respectful,” Mrs. Sowerby objected. “You have never known me to bestow a NICKNAME upon a minister.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0014 }

Nell concealed a grin.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0015 }

“Indeed, Isolde, Gideon, little Gideon, and Small Nell Lucinda are present—along with Odette Pullen. My desire would be to invite Miss Stacey, Aunt Euphemia, Honora, and Mabel as well. Nevertheless, Mabel resides in Vancouver, Nonie has moved to Japan, Miss Stacey is wed and living in California, and Aunt Euphemia, despite her fear of snakes, has traveled to India so she can investigate the mission field of her daughter. How individuals become dispersed across the world is truly terrible.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0016 }

“The Lord never intended it, that’s what,” declared Mrs. Agatha with authority. “During my youth, folk reached adulthood and wedded and took up residence where they had been born, or fairly close to it. Thank goodness you have remained on the Island, Nell. I worried that Hugh would demand to hurry away to the furthest corners of the world upon finishing college, and pull you along with him.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0017 }

“Locations would become crowded in a short time, Mrs. Sowerby, if each person remained in the place of his birth.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0018 }

“Oh, I won’t debate this with you, Nell. A B.A. is something I am not. At what hour of the day will the ceremony take place?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0019 }

“It is noon that we have chosen—high noon, as it is phrased by the society reporters. From then, we will possess sufficient time for catching the evening train bound for Glen St. Agnes.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0020 }

“And the wedding will take place in the parlor?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0021 }

“No—not unless there is rain. It is our intention to be wed in the orchard—with the blue sky above us and the sunshine surrounding us. If it were possible, do you know the time and place I would choose to be married? It would occur at dawn—a June dawn, accompanied by a magnificent sunrise, and roses flowering in the gardens; and I would quietly go down and join Hugh, and the two of us would walk together to the center of the beech woods,—and in that spot, beneath the green arches which would resemble a grand cathedral, our marriage would take place.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0022 }

A disdainful sniff came from Thirza, while a look of shock appeared on Mrs. Sowerby.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0023 }

“However, that would be exceedingly strange, Nell. Indeed, it would hardly appear lawful. Furthermore, what would be the reaction of Mrs. Gorham Pullen?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0024 }

“Ah, that is the difficulty,” Nell sighed. “A great many actions in this existence remain undone simply owing to our dread of Mrs. Gorham Pullen’s remarks. ‘'Tis true, ’tis pity, and pity ’tis, ’tis true.’ What wonderful activities we could engage in if Mrs. Gorham Pullen did not exist!”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0025 }

“At times, Nell, I am not entirely certain that I completely comprehend you,” Mrs. Sowerby grumbled.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0026 }

“In fairness, Nell possessed a romantic nature,” Thirza offered by way of excuse.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0027 }

“Well, wedded existence will in all probability heal her of it,” Mrs. Agatha replied consolingly.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0028 }

Nell chuckled and stole off toward Linger Lane, the spot where Hugh discovered her; and it appeared that neither one harbored much dread, or expectation, that their life together in wedlock would rid them of romance.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0029 }

The individuals from Echo Cottage arrived during the following week, filling Grey Shutters with the excitement of their presence. Miss Rosalind was so unchanged that the three years following her previous Island trip could have been merely a watch in the night; Nell, however, was breathless with wonder regarding Cedric. Was it possible that this impressive six-foot man was the small Cedric from the Brierley school period?
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0030 }

“Cedric, you truly cause me to feel aged,” remarked Nell. “How about that, I am forced to look upward at you!”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0031 }

“Teacher, you will never age,” Cedric remarked. “You belong to those lucky human beings who discovered and imbibed the Fountain of Youth,—you alongside Mother Rosalind. Look at this! After you get married, calling you Mrs. Carrow is something I WILL NOT do. For me, your name will forever be 'Teacher’—the instructor who gave me the finest lessons I was ever taught. There is something I want you to see.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0032 }

That “something” proved to be a pocketbook filled with poems. Cedric had turned a number of his lovely imaginings into poetry, and the editors of magazines had not shown the lack of appreciation that people occasionally attribute to them. Nell perused the poems of Cedric with genuine joy. Charm and promise abounded within them.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0033 }

“Cedric, you are going to be celebrated one day. It was ever my ambition to instruct a single renowned student. My expectation was a university head—yet an extraordinary poet would surpass that. In the future, I will have the chance to brag about beating the renowned Cedric Stanhope. Although, I did not actually beat you, did I, Cedric? That was a wasted chance! Nevertheless, I believe I forced you to stay inside during recess.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0034 }

“It is possible that you are well-known as well, Teacher. Over these past three years, I have come across much of what you have done.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0035 }

“No. I am aware of my own capabilities. I am able to compose lovely, imaginative brief pieces that delight youngsters and prompt editors to mail agreeable payments. However, I am incapable of producing anything grand. The sole opportunity I have for lasting fame in this world is a space within your Memoirs.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0036 }

Belinda the Fourth no longer wore the blue bows, although her freckles remained just as visible.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0037 }

“I certainly never believed I would descend to taking a Yankee as my husband, Miss Harcourt, ma’am,” she stated. “However, what lies ahead remains a mystery, and he cannot be blamed for it. He was simply born as one.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0038 }

“Belinda, because you have taken a Yankee for a husband, you are now a Yankee too.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0039 }

“I am NOT, Miss Harcourt, ma’am! Even if a dozen Yankees became my husbands, I still would not be! There is a certain niceness to Tom. Furthermore, it occurred to me that I ought not to be overly picky, since a second opportunity might never come my way. Between his meals, Tom does not grumble about having to labor, nor does he take to drink, and taking everything into account, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I am contented.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0040 }

“Is Leonora the name he uses for you?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0041 }

“Gracious, no, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. I would not have any idea who he was referring to if he did. Naturally, at the time we were wed he was required to recite, 'I take thee, Leonora,’ and I swear to you, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I have carried the most terrible impression ever since that he was not speaking to me and I have not been properly wedded whatsoever. And thus you are about to be wedded your own self, Miss Harcourt, ma’am? I ever imagined I should enjoy being wed to a physician. It would be exceedingly useful whenever the little ones contracted measles and croup. Tom is merely a bricklayer, yet he possesses a truly fine disposition. When I remarked to him, says I, 'Tom, may I attend Miss Harcourt’s wedding? I intend to go regardless, yet I should prefer to possess your permission,’ he simply responds, 'Suit yourself, Belinda, and you’ll suit me.’ That is a truly agreeable sort of spouse to possess, Miss Harcourt, ma’am.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0042 }

It was the day prior to the nuptials when Cressida and her Reverend Ez came to Grey Shutters. Nell and Cressy shared an ecstatic reunion that soon settled into an intimate, warm conversation regarding everything that had occurred and everything that was on the verge of happening.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0043 }

“Queen Nell, your majesty remains unchanged. I have grown dreadfully skinny following the arrival of the infants. My looks are not nearly as pleasant as before; however, I believe Ez prefers it this way. You see, the difference in our appearances is no longer so sharp. Furthermore, oh, your upcoming marriage to Hugh is absolutely wonderful. Cyril Lisle would have been completely unsuitable, completely. Although I experienced terrible disappointment back then, I am able to recognize that now. You must admit, Nell, your treatment of Cyril was exceedingly poor.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0044 }

“I gather he has gotten better,” Nell smiled.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0045 }

“Oh, yes. He has a wife, and she is a sweet little thing, and their happiness is complete. All things work together for good. That is stated by Ez and the Bible, which are fairly reliable authorities.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0046 }

“Have Hector and Orlando gotten married yet?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0047 }

“Hector is, though Orlando isn’t. Talking with you brings back those sweet past times at Tabby’s Place so vividly, Nell! We enjoyed such great fun!”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0048 }

“Did you visit Tabby’s Place recently?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0049 }

“Indeed, my visits are frequent. Miss Tabby alongside Miss Maria continue sitting near the hearth to do their knitting. That brings to mind—there is a marriage present for you that we carried from those two, Nell. Try to deduce its identity.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0050 }

“I was always unable to. In what way were they aware that my marriage was about to take place?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0051 }

“Oh, I informed them. My visit occurred last week. They showed such great interest, in fact. Miss Tabby sent me a note two days back requesting that I drop by; she then inquired whether I'd bring her present to you. What item from Tabby’s Place would you desire above all else, Nell?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0052 }

“Is it possible that I have been sent her china dogs by Miss Tabby?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0053 }

“Ascend to the top. This exact second, they are inside my trunk. Furthermore, I possess a note intended for you. Hold on a second while I fetch it.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0054 }

“Dear Miss Harcourt,” was what Miss Tabby had penned, “Maria and I found the news of your coming marriage extremely interesting. You have our finest wishes. Neither Maria nor I have ever taken a husband, yet we hold no bias against the matrimony of others. Our china dogs are being dispatched to you. My original plan was to bequeath them to you upon my death, since you appeared to hold a genuine fondness for them. However, Maria and I anticipate remaining above ground for a considerable time still (D.V.), which has led me to choose to bestow the dogs upon you during your youth. Surely it remains in your memory that Gog’s gaze is directed rightward and Magog’s leftward.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0055 }

“Only imagine those beautiful old dogs resting near the hearth in my dream house,” Nell remarked with delight. “I had not anticipated anything quite so wonderful.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0056 }

During that evening, activity buzzed through Grey Shutters as everyone readied for the next day, yet Nell quietly crept off into the dusk. On this final afternoon of her youth, she possessed a small journey to undertake, one that required her to be by herself. Making her way to the small Brierley cemetery beneath the shadow of poplars, she visited Obed’s grave, where she held a quiet rendezvous with eternal loves and bygone memories.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0057 }

“How happy Obed would be tomorrow if he were present,” she murmured. “However, I feel he truly knows and is happy about it—in another place. I’ve read in some place that 'our dead are never dead until we have forgotten them.’ Obed will not ever be dead to me, because I am unable to ever forget him.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0058 }

Placing the flowers she had brought upon his grave, she made her way slowly down the long hill. The evening was gracious, abounding in delightful lights and shadows. Clouds of mackerel filled the western sky—tinted with crimson and amber, separated by long strips of apple-green sky. Farther off lay the shimmering glow of a sea at sunset, and the unceasing sound of many waters rose from the tawny beach. Surrounding her entirely, resting in the refined, lovely quiet of the countryside, were the hills, fields, and woods that she had known and cherished for so long.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0059 }

“History repeats itself,” Hugh stated, coming alongside her when she went by the Carrow gate. “Nell, do you recall our initial journey down this hill—which was, in fact, our very first walk together anywhere?”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0060 }

“As dusk fell, I was returning from the grave of Obed—when you stepped through the gate; whereupon I set aside the pride I had held for years and addressed you.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0061 }

“And all heaven opened before me,” Hugh added. “From that point on I anticipated the next day. When I departed from you at your gate that evening and strolled home I was the most joyful youth on earth. Nell had forgiven me.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0062 }

“It seems to me that your burden of forgiveness was the greatest. I behaved as a miserable, unappreciative child—even following the moment when you truly rescued me on the pond that afternoon. In the beginning, how I detested that heavy weight of debt! The joy I have received is more than I merit.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0063 }

Hugh let out a laugh and squeezed more firmly the young hand wearing his band. A band of pearls formed Nell’s engagement ring. A diamond was something she had declined to wear.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0064 }

“Ever since learning that diamonds were not the beautiful purple I had imagined, I have never truly cared for them. They shall forever remind me of my past letdown.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0065 }

“Yet the ancient tale holds that pearls signify tears,” Hugh had protested.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0066 }

“That does not frighten me. Furthermore, weeping can stem from joy just as easily as from grief. Indeed, my most joyful times occurred with tears filling my eyes—the moment Thirza informed me that I could remain at Grey Shutters—the moment Obed presented me with my first beautiful dress—the moment news reached me that you would pull through the fever. Therefore, bestow pearls upon me for our troth ring, Hugh, and I will gladly take the grief of existence alongside its happiness.”
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0067 }

Yet on this evening, no thoughts of grief entered the minds of our lovers, who focused solely on happiness. Indeed, the next morning would bring their marriage, and the misty, purple coast of Seven Gulls Harbor held the home of dreams that was expecting them.
{: #nw-v04-c03-p0068 }
